en:
You settled in Tsarath quickly, managing to find a quiet place to live somewhere people wouldn't ask a lot of questions.

Your time spent struggling for survival on the island seemed like a distant nightmare, and the familiar rhythm of calm daily life welcomed you once again.

en:
Bato, a small man even by human standards, had difficulty finding work in a nation already oversaturated with strong orcish labourers.

He eventually found a labour commune that was willing to take him in, and he worked hard to earn his keep, but found it more difficult to earn the respect of his peers.

He frequently suffered abuse of all sorts at their hands, and eventually, he left, choosing a solitary life over the constant ridicule.

You have not heard from him since.

en:
Bato, a devoted friend to the very core, was always close at hand once you arrived in Tsarath.

Though he sometimes bordered on overbearing, he always put on a bright face and kept after you to take care of yourself, and having him nearby made the transition into your new life easier.

He made a point of helping out with repairs, construction, and hunting in your new home whenever an opportunity arose, and eventually attracted the attention of a few bright-eyed young orcs who follow him around like lost pups.

He managed to shape them up into a freelance labour crew, and seems happy to be at the center of their attention.

en:
Though he helped with building the boat, Beauregard was unwilling to leave behind the only home he had ever known, and he did not make the journey to Tsarath with you.

He remained on Lukatt and moved into Spartill Lodge, one of the few remaining familiar places to him, and is presumably still there, making a place for himself among the people who still dwell on the island.

en:
Seeing his whole world in shambles was painful for him, so convincing Beauregard to come to Tsarath with you was not difficult. He had even been there once before, hundreds of years past, and seemed eager to see their progress.

He eventually found himself a place in one of the many Tsarathi military schools, where spending his time training and parenting the young orc boys seemed to soothe his confusion, and his mood lightened considerably in the years that followed.

He never had a chance at marrying, but surrounded as he is by his adopted nephews, his life is a happy one.

en:
When your band began work on the boat, Borfalgor, unsure of your destination or your motivations, disappeared one night and did not return.

Presumably, he has returned to whatever it was he was doing before you found him, living his life on the island where he was born.

en:
Borfalgor was eager to see the world outside of Lukatt, and made the journey to Tsarath with you, unafraid of the consequences.

Though his reception in Tsarath was not exactly warm, he was for the most part tolerated.

One day in the marketplace, thanks to his keen eye for jewelry, he spotted a trader selling fake stones and managed to very publicly prove the man's fraud. He was approached by a merchant and offered an ongoing job overseeing and appraising valuables.

He draws a lot of business to the shop on his novelty alone, and he gets to see an endless parade of priceless treasures brought before him, all without having to leave his lavish accomodations, and he seems happy with the place he has found himself.

en:
Since she had come to Lukatt voluntarily, when you arrived in Tsarath, Borgnina immediately began to make arrangements for transport on another ship bound for Crest.

She returned to her previous community in order to announce the success of her pilgrimage, but then quickly requested transfer to another hamlet, where she has settled back into old patterns, serving as an agent of law and faith.

en:
Borgnina threw away her raiments before the boat landed in Tsarath. Though her faith in her God was shaken, her faith in her order had been long since exhausted, and she no longer wished to identify with them.

Instead, she took it upon herself to exemplify her faith personally, and live her life more freely than she had before.

She took a home in a slum by choice, and tried her best to be an uplifting influence to the downtrodden people who surround her, and after a few years, she even married a strong orc who adored her adamant spirit.

Life for Borgnina is not how she imagined it, but she claims she has no regrets.

en:
Despite the danger, Byrne came with you on the boat to Tsarath, eager to leave the memory of his time with Frico behind him.

Wrapped in white robes, he hid in a leper colony where he thought nobody would look for a vampire, and he was so shocked by the understanding welcome he was given, he decided to make his permanent home there.

He subsists on the blood of wildlife and of grateful volunteers, and he serves quietly as the colony's protector and their connection to the outside world.

en:
Byrne returned to Frico's service when you left the island.

He quietly did as he was told for many years thereafter, bringing Frico many guests, some to meet their fortunes, and others to meet their doom.

en:
Byrne wasn't particularly interested in leaving Lukatt, so when the boat left, he stayed behind.

He haunts the woodlands of Knightwood still, preying on the wildlife and unsuspecting travelers as it suits him, and relishing his freedom.

en:
After arriving in Tsarath, Logus contacted a few people who had heard of him, and managed to get signed on with a privateering crew as a ship's mate.

He wasn't thrilled about having to take orders from someone else, but given the choice, he decided that it was more worth it to be out on the water than not, and as far as you know, he is still with that crew, running odd shipments for merchant houses.

en:
Logus stuck close to you when you arrived in Tsarath. He still had sympathetic contacts there, so he managed to find you shelter and work early on, and generally made the transition to your new surroundings much more agreeable.

After a time, he began to feel the call of the sea once again, so he pulled some strings and eventually got put in charge of another ship working for a private merchant corps.

He still tries to stay in touch with you when he can, but he is happy to be back in his element.

en:
Grant was reluctant to board the ship at first, but after a heart-to-heart talk, he decided that he could always return later, and nervously left his homeland behind him.

More than able to keep pace with the orcs of Tsarath in terms of physical strength, he busied himself with being generally helpful, and eventually made himself a fixture on the docks in the town where you landed.

He often wondered aloud about how long he should stay and about what he would say to his father when he went home, but one day, one of the other workers at the dock confessed to having feelings for him, and the talk of going home disappeared overnight.

They live together now in a cabin they built themselves, and Grant's gruff demeanor seems to have softer corners.

en:
Disgusted with your broken promise, Grant left your company as soon as you made it clear that you would be leaving the island.

Rather than face the shame of returning to Hayill empty-handed, Grant gathered up a few of his werewolf friends and staged an assault of his own on Frico's castle.

Many on both sides were slain, including Grant himself, but Frico survived, and declared open war on the island's lycanthropes.

The Knightwood region is now a deadly warzone, with fangs and claws lashing out from behind every shadow, and until one side is exterminated, it seems likely to stay that way.

en:
Grant returned to Hayill to share in the celebrations over the death of Frico.

With the vampire lord vanquished, Hayill quickly became the dominant power on the island, and set up a rogue coalition between the most prominent towns.

Grant is still there, his heroic deed done, watching the development of the island from the front line.

en:
Satisfied to be out of immediate danger, Greave soon made arrangements to return to the Crest mainland and report on what he had seen.

He seemed confident that use of the stocks would cease once it became clear that escape was now possible, but when he tried to inform people what had happened, he was quickly tried as a deserter and found guilty.

He is now interned somewhere on the mainland.

en:
Knowing that returning to Crest would be the end of him, Greave instead tried to get the word out about the atrocities of the island by notifying the Tsarathi authorities through anonymous missives.

When the authorities failed to do anything about it, he took on the moniker "Crowquill" and began distributing stories of events on the island to the public at large, leaving them in busy places and generally making himself impossible to find.

Though nothing has been done in an official capacity, he buries a wry smile in his beard as he hears customers gossiping about his latest pages at the smithy where he works, and people have begun independantly copying and spreading his work around.

Eventually, he tells you, something will snap.

en:
Greening faced some significant culture shock when trying to integrate into Tsarathi life, finding little demand for his passionately-produced pastries.

Settling for crafts gradually further and further from his heart, he eventually found a place in a butcher, where his careful eye for detail goes largely unappreciated.

He gives away his conjured cookies for free, hoping they will catch on, but so far the only real demand comes from odd gangs of poor children.

en:
Not finding much demand for his pastries in Tsarath, Greening was nonetheless determined to make an impression on his stubborn orc hosts.

He shifted his focus onto grilling, and through practice and arcane taboo, he was soon able to serve up a rack of barbequed ribs that even an ogre would swoon over.

He now wages open war against empty orc bellies in his popular grill pit, where he serves strong sauce and stronger beer, and to his delight, he even manages to move a few baskets of butter biscuits now and then.

en:
Used to being surrounded by humans, Kirilo was was accustomed to being stronger than his peers, but in Tsarath where competition for status is fierce, he found himself to be actually quite slight in comparison to his fellow orcs.

When trying to stop a thief in the market one day, he found himself hopelessly outmatched, and was badly beaten. In the weeks that followed, poor medical care resulted in his condition worsening, and he spent his final night alone in an alley in an impoverished slum, his spirit as broken as his body.

en:
Kirilo, feeding his ever-present need to fight for the downtrodden, found his place in Tsarath at one of the many orphanages, where his kind and selfless attitude was quickly appreciated.

He earns coin by working as a runner most days, and then returns home to his boys and to a gaffer who is growing more fond of him by the day.

It isn't nearly as dramatic a life as he is used to, but he concedes that perhaps he has had enough life and death drama for one lifetime, and seems content to settle down.

en:
Leftie was helpful and enthusiastic about repairing the boat, but on the morning you were ready to leave, he told you he wouldn't be coming.

Still unwilling to speak of his crimes, he only said that he was better off on Lukatt, and would not be dissuaded.

He wished you well and stood on the beach as you left, waving you off, and that was the last you ever saw or heard of him.

en:
Initially, Leftie did not want to get on the boat, claiming that it was better for him to just stay and be forgotten.

When you tried to convince him, he got agitated, and you fought in the sand.

You punched him and told him you weren't leaving him behind, and he held you and wept, with the rest of your band awkwardly trying not to stare.

Before long, you were gliding out to sea with Leftie by your side, his swollen black eye shining with appreciation.

en:
In the years thet followed, Leftie was always close by, backing your every move and decision, and he never forgot that you were the one who had faith in him even when he had none in himself.

He seemed wholly unbothered by a life of hard labour in his new home among the orcs of Tsarath, and he made a point of living somewhere nearby, and scarcely went more than a few days without at least stopping in to see how you were doing.

Though he always had a quick temper, he was also loyal and quick to forgive, and you never observed Leftie to be the monster he claimed to be.

en:
Moria left after your battle with Leviathan was over, saying she had no interest in going back to the mainland.

She packed up her meager things and headed off into the wilds of Lukatt alone, where she takes great satisfaction in her daily struggles to survive.

en:
Although she had no love for the idea of returning to civilization, you managed to convince Moria that Tsarath would offer ample opportunities for a survivalist lifestyle, and she agreed to make the journey with you.

Nearly immediately upon arrival, she set out for Tsarath's rugged tundra frontiers, and took up company with a band of loosely-affiliated nomads, moving from place to place as the seasons turned, and earning their living by the sweat of their labour.

You only saw her once after that, but she was still strong, healthy, and glad to be living a life that she felt she had properly earned.

en:
Nazar was obviously distressed at the idea of going back to Tsarath, but he held your hand tightly as the view of the island grew distant across the water.

When you arrived at the mainland, he was surprised to find the Tsarathi commonfolk showing a great deal of support and sympathy for those bearing the scapegoat brand.

Without the need to live a secluded life, Nazar became a social member of the rural community where the two of you lived, and you were eventually married in a small temple, according to Tsarathi traditions.

You live together in a cottage that you built with help from your neighbors, and your life is both simple and fulfilling.

en:
Nazar helped you make preparations for the trip, but refused to return to Tsarath, saying he preferred to remain on Lukatt instead.

He went to Greenback Bay, where he found himself high in demand on labour teams and guard teams, as well as in the arms of lonely castaways, and is as happy there as he has ever been.

en:
Torn between his dislike of Tsarathi laws and the idea of losing you to them, Nazar nervously accompanied you back to the mainland.

Though he had grown up in one of the Tsarathi military schools, he had no family to speak of and no real place to go back to, so he stuck close by your side, an obvious affection for you shining through his every move.

He was eventually able to find steady work as woodsman, and made his permanent home as close to you as he could manage.

Indeed, it became hard to remember a time when Nazar's affection and support were not a constant feature of your life.

en:
Paul was happy to have been helpful with your survival, but he mostly got in the way when it came to repairing the boat, and he eventually decided that his time with you was at an end.

He made a home for himself near Spartill Lodge, where he continues to work the forests for anyone willing to pay him for his time.

en:
Paul was excited to be part of all the activity surrounding your departure, and it wasn't until you were out at sea already that he started having second thoughts.

You managed to talk him down, however, and when you finally arrived in Tsarath, Paul drew less attention than he had expected.

Though not exactly common, many of the people there had seen their share of giants already, and when he made himself available for labour jobs, he quickly found himself with as much work as he could handle.

Being part of a community was a new experience for Paul, but he found it to his liking, and he soon moved into a permanent home of his own construction in a small frontier town, where he remains busy and content.

en:
Once you arrived in Tsarath, Peregrine began burgling again almost immediately.

He quickly found, however, that without his previous network of contacts, the profession was much more dangerous than he was accustomed to, and a persistent manhunt for him has been on ever since his first heist.

His life is spent nervously hiding from bootsteps in mouldering hovels and sleeping with one eye open.

en:
Peregrine had previously spent a great deal of time working as a sailor as a cover for his burgling, and he took your move to Tsarath as an opportunity to embrace that work full-time.

It didn't take him long to secure a position working on a merchant ship, and he is now well-paid to make shipping runs back and forth for some of the very people he used to burgle.

Though he sometimes complains that he misses the excitement, he adds that not having to constantly look over his shoulder and fear for his safety is a nice perk, and he seems content in the choices he has made.

Whenever he is in port, he makes a point of checking up on you and stopping by to share a bottle of whatever expensive liquor he has managed to stow away.

en:
Rangda refused to return to Tsarath, and left your company as soon as you found the boat.

She eventually made her way to Marsaven on the southeast side of the island and decided to settle in, but has had difficulty making friends, as many of the people there have little patience for her attitude.

She is still finding herself, but does not regret leaving her old life behind.

en:
She deliberated on the issue for quite a while, but ultimately, Rangda decided to remain on Lukatt instead of returning to Tsarath, knowing that she would eventually be subject to the familiar confines of the law once again.

She saw you off on the beach and then made her way to Marsaven, where she worked hard to prove herself to the people there and integrate into the community, and eventually became a guardsman.

Life on Lukatt isn't easy for her, but when she wakes up and straps on her uniform each day, she feels as though she's made the right decision.

en:
Rosaline seemed to be nervous about making the journey to Tsarath, and so she ultimately decided to stay on Lukatt.

She said that there would be other boats eventually, since the seas had been calmed, and that she wanted time to think about what her next move would be.

She ended up going to the Pumphouse Brewery in the Bracewind region and entertaining guests who were accustomed to long waiting periods.

en:
Upon arriving in Tsarath, Rosaline did exactly what she said she would do; she found herself a bawdy, bustling tavern and refused to leave until they hired her on as a dancer.

More than capable of handling herself in a rough crowd, she now dances burlesque to the delight of throngs of merrily drunken orcs, and finds herself rather fond of the attention she gets.

She now makes plenty enough coin in tips to clothe herself in lavish silks and fine jewelry, and has a long list of devoted admirers.

She still worries that someday her old troupe will catch up with her, but for the time being, she is meeting life head-on and having a lot of fun in the process.

en:
Shapiro found acceptance in Tsarath almost immediately, offering his services to a cabal of independant sorcerers.

Finding their rules much less restrictive than those of the Crest guilds he was used to, he merrily buries himself in research and experimentation, earning a more or less honest wage, and swearing that he should have come to Tsarath years ago.
